title: Workload Intelligence: Workload-Aware IaaS abstraction for Cloud Efficiency
problem: Cloud platforms lack visibility into workload characteristics beyond basic VM type information, limiting the ability to optimize resource allocation, customize platform behavior, and enable workloads to react to platform events. This narrow interface results in VM type proliferation, suboptimal resource utilization, and missed optimization opportunities.
motivation: Modern cloud infrastructure suffers from information asymmetry between workloads and platforms. Workloads cannot take advantage of platform insights (e.g., impending VM eviction), and platforms cannot leverage workload characteristics (e.g., availability requirements) for better resource management and cost savings.
method: Workload Intelligence (WI) proposes a bidirectional communication framework enabling dynamic information exchange between cloud workloads and platforms. The framework allows workloads to declare characteristics and platforms to expose optimization hints and platform events.
key_novelty: First comprehensive framework for bidirectional workload-platform communication in cloud IaaS, enabling dynamic workload adaptation and platform-aware resource allocation.
contributions: Framework architecture for bi-directional communication between workloads and platforms
Mechanism for declaring workload characteristics (e.g., low availability requirements)
Platform event signaling (e.g., pre-eviction notifications) for workload adaptation
Abstraction layer reducing VM type complexity through workload-aware customization

metrics.focus: Cost efficiency, resource utilization, workload responsiveness
metrics.measurement: Presumed: VM reconfiguration time, platform adaptation latency, cost per workload

limitations: Abstract only - lacks concrete implementation details, performance numbers, and evaluation results
